Leaders' visions, however, are not solely a matter of perceived utility, the affective reaction of the leader's vision in plans is also of
some importance. Table 6 presents the results obtained in the analysis of covariance examining the effects of the manipulations on
affective reaction. It was found that intelligence (F(1, 295) = 7.09, p ≤.01), conscientiousness (F(1, 295) = 9.86), and extraversion
(F(1, 295) = 3.92, p ≤.05) were all signiﬁcant covariates being positively related to the production of leader plans evidencing high
affective reaction. Moreover, the signiﬁcant (F(1, 295) = 6.15, p ≤.05) positive relationship produced by leader style indicated
that charismatic leaders formulated more emotionally engaging plans while those who had more experience in leadership roles
were also likely to produce plans evidencing signiﬁcantly (F(1, 295) = 9.62, p ≤.01) greater affective reaction.
Again, a signiﬁcant (F(1, 325) = .806, p ≤.01) main effect was obtained for cases. In support of Hypothesis 1, it was found that

affective reaction. Similarly, a signiﬁcant (F(1, 325) = 4.60, p ≤.05) main effect was obtained for schema. Here, in support of
